ok_upper_mount_scott.blurb: Upper Mount Scott is a compact granite crag on the flank of Mount Scott in the Wichita Mountains. Most of the climbing is short, mostly traditional lines, with a few top-ropes and a handful of boulder problems mixed in. Grades cluster between 5.6 and 5.10, which makes it one of the friendlier places in the Wichitas to learn to place gear, with a small number of harder pitches in the 5.11s and a single 5.12 for those who want a challenge. Because the road reaches the summit, the walk in is brief, though the walls here are not tall. Expect company on busy weekends.
ok_upper_mount_scott.approach: Leave the car at the very west end of the summit parking area, walk a short way back down the paved road, then step over the guardrail onto the path that drops to the base of the crag.

ok_zoo_wall.blurb: Zoo Wall is a granite face in The Narrows, the canyon cragging zone of the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge. Nearly everything here is traditional, with some top-rope lines and a lone aid route. Grades run from 5.6 up to the low 5.12s, but the bulk of the lines are 5.8 through 5.10, so a rack and some experience are the price of entry. The wall is split into left, middle and right sections, and many climbers come for the moderate crack and dihedral climbing. The approach is a pleasant, well-built trail through the canyon.
ok_zoo_wall.parking_note: Drive west from refuge headquarters and take the turn toward Dog Run; roughly two miles beyond the gate, the picnic area on your left, outside the gate, is where you leave the car. The canyon trail begins at the picnic area's east end.

ok_little_bugaboo_creek.blurb: Little Bugaboo Creek is a bouldering zone at McGee Creek in southeastern Oklahoma, spread along a long band of sandstone cliff and boulders in the woods. The rock is generally good, especially on the problems that see regular traffic, while quieter walls can need a brush. Grades run from V0 through the low V4 to V6 range, where much of it sits, up to a couple of V11 roofs, and the roof problems are the draw for strong boulderers. Some walls collect plenty of crash pads on a good weekend. Finding the cliff takes a little attention, so follow the trail description rather than a state park route.
ok_little_bugaboo_creek.parking_note: Search for the ranger station using a map pin placed on the bouldering rather than a state park address, which sends you to the wrong place. The trailhead lot lies a few minutes of driving past the station.

ok_horse_corral_face.blurb: Horse Corral Face is the busiest wall at Robbers Cave State Park in the Sans Bois hills of eastern Oklahoma. The rock is tight, dense sandstone with ironstone flakes, good enough to take nuts and cams. Top-roping dominates, with a good number of traditional lines and a few boulder problems beside them. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.10, with a scattering of easier and harder ones, so it works well for newer climbers building skills and for groups. Anchors are often trees or boulders set back from the lip, so bring enough rope and be comfortable building your own.
ok_horse_corral_face.parking_note: Follow the main park road in toward the Robbers Cave trailhead and use the lot there. A short path leads to the climbing from the lot.

ok_09_watch_me_wall.blurb: Watch Me Wall is one of the numbered climbing areas on Baldy Point at Quartz Mountain, a big granite dome on the western end of the Wichita Mountains. The style here is the area's trademark friction climbing on smooth, steep rock, mostly traditional with a smaller share of bolted lines. Several bolted routes carry long runouts, so treat them as bold rather than as casual sport climbs. Grades mostly span 5.8 to 5.11, with a few easier and a few harder. The wall catches sun for most of the day, which makes cooler months the comfortable choice, and the walk from the lot is short.
ok_09_watch_me_wall.parking_note: Use the lot next to the picnic tables at the foot of Baldy Point, on the southwest side of the formation.

ok_lost_dome_main_area.blurb: Lost Dome is a remote granite dome tucked behind the Crab-Eyes boulders in Charon's Garden, deep in the Wichita Mountains. The south-facing main wall holds a mix of traditional and bolted lines, from 5.6 up to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range and one aid line. It rewards a bit of route-finding and a real walk in, so it stays quiet compared with the roadside crags. With a south face it soaks up sun, which suits cooler months and is hot in summer. Good for a full day away from the crowds.
ok_lost_dome_main_area.approach: Follow the Charon's Garden trail west until the dome comes into view just northeast of you, then circle its east side to the base of the south-facing wall. Crab-Eyes boulders help locate it.
